evidence.source: Multi-function Chinese Character Database, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: Oracle-bone character entry; paleographic account and cited inscriptions
evidence.text: The database describes 日 as a depiction of the sun, with early round forms sometimes squared because a circle was difficult to carve on bone; it says the central mark distinguished the graph from 囗. It cites Shang oracle-bone examples for the sun and sunrise (合集34163), eclipse (合集11480), daylight contrasted with evening (合集33871, 合集34036), and a period of five days (合集12314). It also notes later bronze-inscription uses for the sun, daylight, and calendar-day unit. The inscription citations substantiate distinct early uses; they do not by themselves establish the order in which those senses developed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：日

evidence.text: The entry provides examples under oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscripts, seal script, and Shuowen headings, and states that 日 resembles the sun and its original meaning is the sun. The page identifies a bronze example as inscription 集成05990. Its displayed categories support a broad sequence of attested script traditions, but the accessible text does not supply dates for each individual form.
evidence.title: 漢字「日」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, digitized 說文解字 with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.field: 卷七 日部 entry and commentary
evidence.text: Xu Shen's entry defines 日 as 實, describes it as 太陽之精不虧, analyzes it as 从囗一 and calls it pictographic. Duan Yucai explains the outer shape as the sun's outline and the inner stroke as its undiminished center. This is the received Han-era account, not direct evidence for the graph's earliest form; the oracle-bone material provides earlier evidence.
evidence.title: 說文解字「日」

evidence.field: Unihan database documentation and lookup behavior
evidence.text: Unicode's Unihan documentation says the database distributes character data including readings, describes Unihan field files and their tab-separated record format, and directs users to the interactive lookup interface. A direct character-specific lookup for 日 was attempted but timed out; therefore this documentation does not verify the kMandarin value itself. The supplied local Unihan row is 日 kMandarin rì, but it is not emitted here as externally verified evidence.
evidence.kind: official database documentation; lookup attempt limitation
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, row 日; sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, kMandarin row 日
evidence.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart row is 日, Mandarin rì, Middle Chinese nyit, Old Chinese *C.nik, gloss “sun; day”; these are the dataset's distinct MC and OC columns. The supplied Unihan row is 日 kMandarin rì. These exact local rows were checked, but the character-specific Unicode record URL timed out, so these repository rows cannot be treated as externally verified or as click-through evidence. As this character is a pictogram and no phonetic component is proposed, neither reading provides evidence for a sound-component relationship.
evidence.kind: local structured reading data; external lookup unavailable
evidence.title: Unihan character lookup for U+65E5 (attempted; timeout)

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Academia Sinica evolution page and Shuowen entry. Ctext returned 403 on open. The primary paleographic dictionary query returned Shang inscription references for sun, sunrise, eclipse, daylight, and day-unit uses.

search_audit.query: site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl 日 U+65E5 Unihan rì; site:unicode.org/charts/unihan 日 U+65E5 kMandarin; Baxter Sagart 日 *C.nik nyit 2014 reconstruction; 日 oracle bone inscriptions used for day date Shang occurrences meaning sun day
search_audit.outcome: Inspected Unicode Unihan documentation, the Unicode grid index and the CUHK character entry. Direct U+65E5 lookup was attempted twice and failed, first as inaccessible and then as a timeout. Baxter–Sagart reading checked against exact supplied local row; no independently inspected external table page was located.

gaps: The accessible evidence gives Shang-period inscription identifiers but not a securely dated first occurrence for each distinct use; exact inscription datings remain unverified here.

Semantic ordering should not be inferred from the dictionary's gloss sequence. The primary paleographic reference documents sun, daylight, and day-unit uses in oracle-bone inscriptions, but does not establish a precise transition date from one sense to another.

The reason for the central mark distinguishing 日 from 囗 is a source's paleographic explanation; possible histories of individual graphic variants or scribal changes beyond this broad sequence were not established.

The received Shuowen component analysis 从囗一 is a historical interpretation. Earlier inscriptional evidence supports a sun pictogram but does not independently establish that its original structure consisted of semantic components 囗 plus 一.

Unihan's official character-specific lookup failed to load, so the exact upstream kMandarin value rì could not be verified through the requested click-through. The local row is available and checked but is not external evidence.

No sound component applies to this graph. Dossier claims about a whole-graph loan for 入 or assimilation involving 金 concern other lexical/graphical uses and were not established as historical explanations of 日's sun/day graph.
